items.title: A separated flat locally finite type morphism which is an isomorphism over a retrocompact scheme theoretically dense open is an open immersion
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is a Zariski main theorem style criterion: a separated flat locally finite type morphism which is an isomorphism over a retrocompact scheme theoretically dense open is itself an open immersion (statement lines 3072-3081, tag 081M). The proof does real work at each step: it upgrades local finite type to local finite presentation over the dense open, reduces to a quasi-compact flat morphism onto its image over an affine base, uses dimension zero fibres and the etale splitting of the quasi-finite part to write the base change as a finite piece plus a piece empty over the closed fibre, and then kills that second piece by scheme theoretic density, before descending finiteness and comparing the degree with one over the dense open. The density argument is the substance, so the claim is H2.
